requirements.note: Edge-to-edge 3-column grid of square HSL tiles with centred emoji, 600 tiles, newest first, with 1pt gutters like Photos.
System pull-down menu with All Boards plus ten boards and a checkmark. The tile count updates (Night: 58).
Push to a large view with title, board and date. Swiping left/right changes the tile and stays inside the active filter ('1 of 58'). Prev/next buttons too; Previous is disabled on the first tile.
Heart in the nav bar and a 'Like Tile' button both toggle. The Liked tab shows the same grid with heart badges and its own filter and count.
Select/Done mode with circle checkmarks, Select All, a selection count, bulk Like, and Delete behind a confirmation alert.
Bulk likes, a single unlike and a 2-tile deletion all survived relaunch (598 tiles, Liked count correct).

bugs: At the largest text size the filter label breaks inside the word: 'All Board / s' wraps across three lines.
At the largest text size the detail screen's prev/next row falls apart: the Next button wraps onto its own line under Previous.
tells: Generic 'Tile' nav title on the detail screen instead of the tile's name.
The tab bar stays visible on the pushed detail screen, and the large view has a redundant heart in the nav bar plus a full-width 'Like Tile' button.
Select-mode actions are a hand-built grey panel stacked above the tab bar ('3 Selected / Select All / Like / Delete'), not a system toolbar. The grid is cut off abruptly above it.
No large title on the main screens; inline titles only.
Swiping on the detail swaps content instead of paging horizontally with the finger like Photos.
Explanatory 'Swipe the tile to browse' hint text under the controls.
Nav bar titles don't grow with Dynamic Type, while body text grows to the point of breaking.
A.scroll: The 600-tile grid scrolls smoothly under slow drags and hard flings, with no blank or popping rows. The scroll position is kept after opening a tile and after switching tabs, and it bounces normally at both ends.

requirements.note: 3-column grid of rounded square tiles with centred emoji, newest first, filling the width with small margins. A branded header ('Find your mood.') sits above it.
A pill button opens a system menu with All boards plus ten boards and a checkmark. The count updates (Night: 58).
Large view with board, title and 'Added <date>'. A real horizontal paging collection follows the finger and stays inside the active filter. Prev/next arrows and a position count.
A large 'Like this tile' button toggles to 'Liked'. The Liked tab shows the same grid with heart badges, a filter and a count.
Select/Done mode with checkmarks and tinted borders, a selection count, Select all, bulk Like and Delete. Delete asks for confirmation and then offers an Undo banner.
Bulk likes, a single unlike and a 2-tile deletion all survived relaunch (598 tiles, Liked count correct).

bugs: Entering select mode inserts a '3 selected / Select all' row above the grid, which shoves every tile down about 58pt as soon as the first tile is tapped.
tells: Heavily branded, web-like hero header on each tab: a letter-spaced eyebrow ('A PLACE FOR INSPIRATION'), a serif display headline, a subtitle and section labels in place of a system large title.
A decorative app-icon image in a glass circle at the nav bar's leading edge looks like a button but does nothing.
Custom-drawn filter pill and custom capsule bulk-action buttons rather than a toolbar.
The detail nav title is a generic 'Inspiration'.
Custom terracotta accent and cream background instead of system colours. The unselected Liked tab icon is a filled black heart.
Decorative hint and footer copy ('Swipe to find your next favorite', 'A little color goes a long way.').
Nav bar titles don't grow with Dynamic Type, though the content reflows cleanly (the eyebrow and subtitle are dropped at the largest size).
B.scroll: The grid scrolls smoothly under drags and hard flings, with no blank or popping rows. It bounces at both ends and keeps its position across a detail push and tab switches. The detail pager snaps page by page like a native paging collection.

why: Both apps meet all six requirements and persist correctly. A looks more like a stock Photos-style app, but it breaks at the largest text size (a word split in the filter label, a collapsed prev/next row) and its detail view swaps tiles rather than paging. B is more branded and less system-like, but it handles Dynamic Type cleanly, hides the tab bar on detail, has a true paging large view and adds undo after delete, so it feels more finished to use and ship.
